recommendation: Keep this audit commit. Apply any future common-code-system migration or other escape-valve addition under FHIR-56335/FHIR-55336 when those R6 decisions enter source-edit scope.
issue_request: FHIR-13704 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification STU3 Pharmacy issue asking for MedicationRequest.intent to align with RequestIntent because MedicationRequestIntent lacked option for RequestGroup-based chemotherapy regimens. The resolution requested proposal, plan, order, instance-order, and option, while a Jira comment clarified that irrelevant common codes could still be excluded.
initial_application: Git cf35ab7ebcf102964085812bf6e2166fe3eaa11c explicitly applied GF #13704 by changing the MedicationRequest intent value-set content. The patch added option to MedicationRequestIntent and the MedicationRequest.intent short list while retaining the MedicationRequest-specific binding and workflow mapping to Request.intent.
additional_context: MedicationRequest is active in source/fhir.ini and is the successor to MedicationPrescription. Current source includes proposal, plan, order, original-order, reflex-order, filler-order, instance-order, and option in the MedicationRequest intent code system. Later Published Pharmacy issues such as FHIR-13935, FHIR-17680, and FHIR-34218 reviewed/expanded the same code family while retaining MedicationRequest-specific constraints. Newer R6 issues FHIR-56335 and FHIR-55336 are only Resolved - change required and propose future targeted migration to the common Request code system while keeping a MedicationRequest value-set subset.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. Applying FHIR-13704 literally as a generic request-intent value-set binding now would be overbroad because current RequestIntent includes additional codes such as directive, and the later unresolved R6 decisions call for targeted code-system work rather than broadening the value set.
